Starting point
AI system and date: ChatGPT 6.1-Sol 11/6/2026
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.

Our question is “What effects do various musical elements have on the popularity of a music track on Spotify?”. Our initial model is an additive linear model for the effects of certain predictors on a track’s popularity score. The predictors are song duration, key, tempo, whether or not the song is explicit, track genre, and time signature. The baseline result was extensive and found many significant predictors, but the adj. R^2 value was pretty low (0.25). We want to improve our model to get a higher adj. R^2 value and reduce the amount of predictors we have.

title: Spotify Popularity Prediction
text:
The question
** Why are some songs listened across millions of people while some never make it out of someone’s basement? We hope to discover what effects various musical elements have on the popularity of a music track on Spotify, by looking at the level of popularity across the duration of the song, the key, the tempo, the genre, the time signature, and whether or not it is explicit. We believe that this analysis will help music producers make better business decisions, as well as well-known and aspiring artists to produce more popular songs. We will look at 114,000 individual spotify music tracks on a dataset found on kaggle at https://doi.org/10.34740/kaggle/dsv/4372070. It is necessary to note that the process at which songs were given a popularity score seems as if it could be subjective and may not be the best or the only way to measure or predict popularity of a song. **

The question
Why are some songs listened to by millions of people while some never make it out of someone’s basement? We hope to discover what effects various musical elements have on the popularity of a music track on Spotify, by looking at the level of popularity across the duration of the song, the key, the tempo, the genre, the time signature, and whether or not it is explicit. We believe that this analysis will help music producers make better business decisions, as well as well-known and aspiring artists to produce more popular songs. We will look at 114,000 individual Spotify music tracks on a dataset found on kaggle at https://doi.org/10.34740/kaggle/dsv/4372070. It is necessary to note that the exact process at which songs were given a popularity score is based on an algorithm not clearly defined, but involves the total number of plays and how recent those plays are. We are not sure exactly how the scores were produced or if they are 100% accurate, but we will work as if they are.
